system: You are an equity research assistant at a brokerage. Analysts use your summaries to decide quickly whether a news item matters for a specific stock. Accuracy matters more than completeness: never state anything the article does not support.
prompt:
Target stock: Exxon Mobil (XOM)

<article>
HEADLINE: UPDATE 2-Exxon signals fall in fourth-quarter upstream profit

BODY:
(Adds details in paragraphs 4 to 7)

Jan 7 (Reuters) - U.S. oil major Exxon Mobil said on Wednesday that lower crude oil prices could cut its fourth-quarter upstream earnings by about $800 million to $1.2 billion.

Oil prices declined 9.2% during the three months ended December 31, as concerns about oversupply and tariffs outweighed geopolitical risks.

Brent crude futures shed about 19% in 2025, the most substantial annual percentage decline since 2020 and their third straight year of losses, the longest such streak on record. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude logged an annual decline of almost 20%.

The company said in a regulatory filing that changes in gas prices could affect its quarterly upstream earnings from a negative $300 million to as much as a positive $100 million.

Exxon's snapshot is closely watched for clues on how the broader oil sector will fare when companies begin releasing quarterly results in a few weeks.

Analysts expect Exxon to report adjusted earnings of $1.66 per share for the fourth quarter, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The company will release results for the final quarter of the year on January 30, the filing showed.

The energy major had posted $5.7 billion in upstream earnings for the third quarter. (Reporting by Pooja Menon in Bengaluru; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar and Anil D'Silva)
</article>

Instructions:
1. Classify how relevant the article is to XOM:
   - "primary": Exxon Mobil is the main subject.
   - "secondary": Exxon Mobil is one of several subjects, or a key driver of the story.
   - "peripheral": Exxon Mobil is only mentioned in passing.
   - "none": Exxon Mobil is not mentioned; any link would be your own inference.
2. Use only information stated in the article (headline + body). Do not add background knowledge,
   prices or context that is not in the text. If the body is missing or is generic boilerplate,
   rely on the headline and set "information_quality" to "limited".
3. Keep figures (prices, %, $ amounts, dates) exactly as written. Attribute analyst opinions,
   rumours and "sources say" reports as such.
4. Write for an investor in XOM: the event, the key numbers, and why it could matter for the stock.
   If relevance is "peripheral" or "none", say so plainly and cover only what concerns XOM
   (or, if nothing does, the market context in one sentence). Do not invent a connection.

Return only a JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "relevance": "primary" | "secondary" | "peripheral" | "none",
  "event_type": "earnings_guidance" | "analyst_action" | "m_and_a" | "regulatory_legal" | "product_business" | "macro_market" | "management_corporate" | "other",
  "summary": "<= 50 words, focused on XOM",
  "key_facts": ["<= 3 short facts, each <= 15 words, keep figures"],
  "sentiment_for_ticker": "positive" | "negative" | "neutral" | "mixed",
  "sentiment_rationale": "<= 20 words",
  "information_quality": "full" | "limited"
}
